web_evidence.title: Excerpt from The Time Keeper
web_evidence.note: The author’s sustained prologue and opening excerpt narrates Dor, Sarah, Victor, and other characters externally while moving among their private thoughts; occasional “you” and “we” are authorial reader address, not second- or first-person story participation.

web_evidence.title: Mitch Albom Writing Styles in The Time Keeper
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies the novel’s overall viewpoint as third-person omniscient with an authorial voice and explains its movement among Dor, Sarah, and Victor.

web_evidence.title: The Time Keeper Literary Elements
web_evidence.note: The literary-elements guide explicitly describes third-person narration that reveals the thoughts and feelings of all three protagonists.

person_note: The controlling narrator is a nonparticipating third-person authorial narrator who moves among Dor, Sarah, and Victor and accesses their thoughts. Diagnostic quote passages expose external narration, and the authorized opening demonstrates the same structure at sustained length; two whole-book viewpoint descriptions independently confirm it. First-person forms in the quotes occur in dialogue or universal aphorisms, while generic “you” passages address readers rather than a story-specific protagonist. The remaining limitation is that the Tier A prose covers the opening rather than the entire novel, but the whole-book sources and quote evidence agree and no alternating base-person structure was found.
